claim_being_audited: That rejecting the vendor was policy-compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved risk at decision time, even though the record did not prove a formally logged control failure.
specific_concerns: The available record is only the Actor's summary, so the cited evidence cannot be independently checked for content, timing, or materiality.

unsupported_claims: That the cited record, as summarized, definitively establishes reject-level material unresolved risk rather than a need for follow-up or escalation.

evidence_requests: Provide the full text or faithful excerpts of BPROC-032-B, BPROC-032-C, BPROC-032-D, and BPROC-032-E, including dates and authors.
Show the exact procurement language on whether unresolved storage controls required follow-up, escalation, hold, or rejection.
Provide any admissible document that explicitly assesses these issues as a material unresolved risk sufficient for vendor rejection.
Provide the decision record showing whether the action taken was a temporary non-approval pending remediation or a final rejection.
decision_criteria: Reject is compliant only if admissible evidence shows a material unresolved risk, not merely open diligence questions.
Evidence supporting only follow-up, escalation, or conditional non-approval is insufficient for a clean rejection verdict.
No reliance may be placed on private security-review results unless formally logged in the admissible record.
Materiality, unresolved status at the decision time, and the link from those facts to the chosen action must be explicit in the record.
